title: BCBSND Caring Foundation supports veteran mental health through Strike Out the Stigma partnership
text:
BCBSND Caring Foundation supports veteran mental health through Strike Out the Stigma partnership
The Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota (BCBSND) Caring Foundation announced on Aug. 26 that it concluded its fourth season of Strike Out the Stigma, partnering with the Brady Oberg Legacy Foundation to support veteran mental health programs across North Dakota.
Throughout July, the BCBSND Caring Foundation made a donation for every strikeout recorded during home games by six local baseball teams. The more than 600 strikeouts resulted in a $25,000 donation for the Brady Oberg Legacy Foundation. After learning how the foundation helped BCBSND employee John Dalziel navigate life after military service, the Caring Foundation doubled its investment to $50,000.
Dalziel, director of physical security and protection services and a U.S. Marine Corps combat veteran, shared his experiences with mental health struggles following his service and how connecting with fellow veterans through foundation programs provided crucial support. The funding will allow more than 200 veterans to attend adventure retreats at no cost, where they can connect with others who understand their experiences and build lasting support systems.
"As Brady's sister, I know firsthand how important it is to continue breaking the stigma surrounding mental health,” said Tracy Dunham, founder and executive director of the Brady Oberg Legacy Foundation. “We are honored and grateful to partner with Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota. This partnership not only raised funds for our mission but also helps spark important conversation about mental health. Together, we're reminding veterans that asking for help is a sign of strength and that there is always hope." Brady Oberg was a combat veteran whose life was cut short by invisible wounds from war; his family established the foundation in his memory to help other veterans find connection and support.
Amber Blomberg, executive director of the BCBSND Caring Foundation, said: "One of the most meaningful parts of this partnership has been hearing directly from veterans whose lives have been touched by Brady Oberg Legacy Foundation. When one of our own employees shared how important this organization was for him as well as other veterans seeking connection, it reinforced why this work matters. That's why we chose to double our investment this year. Every veteran deserves to know they don't have to face life's challenges alone." Through initiatives like Strike Out the Stigma and Shut Out the Stigma, BCBSND Caring Foundation has supported behavioral health organizations statewide.
Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota works to improve community health through affiliations such as Noridian Healthcare Solutions—which manages government health programs—and foundation efforts supporting sustainable initiatives in communities; it serves hundreds of thousands across North Dakota while offering coverage nationwide and internationally, according to the official website.
